newsitem.title: UK: Chapati foils British mountaineer's record attempt.
newsitem.headline: Chapati foils British mountaineer's record attempt.

text.p: A British climber's attempt to conquer the 14 highest peaks in the world has been foiled -- by a chapati.
Alan Hinkes pulled a muscle in his back while eating the thin unleavened bread on a Himalayan mountainside. Flour on the chapati blew in his face, causing him to sneeze.
"I have never had back problems before but after sneezing I was in agony," Hinkes said by satellite phone from his base camp on Thursday. "I just couldn't move."

Hinkes had already climbed nine of the 14 "8,000" peaks, so called because they rise above 8,000 metres (26,000 feet), and was attempting a world first by climbing the remaining five in the space of 12 months.
But now, immobilised, he is waiting to be airlifted off Nanga Parbat, known locally as the Killer Mountain. To add to his woes, the climber has been robbed of vital equipment by armed locals.
"I am running out of food and petrol," he told Reuters. "I'm very frustrated and angry."
